issue.title: find_gate_shell_by_gate_id keeps full-history/full-tree fallbacks and an index miss silently skips shell settlement
issue.description:
Found by the sase-zr landing audit (sase-zr note #2, gap 6) and detailed in phase bounded-lookup-fallback of the rejected completion plan (plan:202609/sase_zr_completion.md). Deliberately deferred out of the narrowed sase-zr close-out epic by owner decision on 2026-09-16: the indexed exact lookup (sase-core 682dbec) is the hot path and works; the fallbacks only fire on index absence/error, so replacing them carries more regression risk than value right now.

Remaining defects: on index absence or error, find_gate_shell_by_gate_id falls back to a full-history list_gate_shells query and then an entire-artifact-tree scan (audit measured ~7.0 s); index write failures are swallowed in agent_artifact_index_lifecycle_mutations.py, yet an index miss is treated as final, so callers (cli_answer.py, plan_approval_actions.py, mobile) silently skip settle_gate_shell with no signal and no scheduled repair; the one-time v31 index migration decodes every row inside whichever call first opens the index, which can be an interactive click.

Desired remediation (per the sase-zr contract): resolve misses through a verified direct pointer (gate bundle creation receipt / .creation_result.json / envelope shell block) to the exact owning shell, durably schedule index repair and return an explicit settlement-pending result instead of silently skipping, and keep full-decode migrations off interactive callers. Policy changes belong in sase-core.

task_type_fields.impact: Interactive gate answers pay O(archive history) when the index is unhealthy, and a silent settlement skip leaves gate shells unsettled with no repair scheduled, which later surfaces as stale shell state.
task_type_fields.repro: Remove or corrupt the artifact index, then answer a gate: the lookup runs the full-history query plus full-tree scan on the interactive path. Alternatively, make the index return no row for an existing gate id: the caller skips shell settlement silently.
